newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares set to rally on strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: German shares set to rally on strong dollar.

text.p: German shares registered a generally mixed performance in thin pre-bourse tradings, but a strong dollar looked set to boost the IBIS DAX index and analysts were looking at a mid-term target of 3,600 points.

Many market players extended the Ascension Thursday holiday into a long weekend, which had lowered volumes appreciably. By 0800 GMT the IBIS DAX index was up 12.63 points, or 0.36 percent, at 3,550.08 points.
"There are positive factors coming from many sides on the German share market at the moment," Bayerische Vereinsbank said in a research document.
Despite a mauling in recent days, the dollar was still seen as having a positive impact on the German share market in the mid-term.
The currency was stable at around 1.70 marks and Vereinsbank said a rise to 1.75 marks was possible, while the strength of sterling was also helpful.
"These currency trends, combined with the appealing levels of economic growth abroad, should help improve the outlook for the export sector," said Vereinsbank.
"The clear abatement of volumes in recent days is a cause for concern," analysts at Commerzbank said.
